items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: my roommate was Sanborn, Keith Jarrett was there, Peter Erskine was there, Randy, so many guys that ended up playing together over the years.

ctx.x: You know you don’t hear Cannonball so much but I was very lucky — we went to hear Cannonball in Dallas when I was in North Texas and it was when I was first writing. And I wrote a chart called “Codify” which is an abstract sort of 13-bar blues. And we had a great band and Cannonball, I remember that he — of course I don’t remember anything melodically about what he played but I remember he played “Carnival” and he played like 13 choruses. And I had tears in my eyes at the end of it you know. And we went up and…

up. They came up to the school the following day. And so everybody was thrilled and Leon Breedon says, “This is a new chart by Lou Marini.” And we played the chart and when we finished it I looked up and everybody in the band was looking at me. And at first I was like what’s going on. And then I realized that Cannonball and Nat are standing right behind me over my shoulders, and Cannonball leans over to me and he says, “Lou, you a crazy motherfucker.” And you know we became friends. And I ran into him like with…

Yeah. I got to play with him a few times in the educational settings and I felt so good about putting him in front of school kids. Like he was a role model in many ways. I’m going to test your memory a little bit. If you go to Wikipedia, your Wikipedia page, it has a very lengthy list of recordings you’ve played on, and I think it ends like ten years ago. But do you remember — I’m going to ask you a couple of things. Do you remember 1981 Peter Tosh, “Wanted Dread or Alive”?
